scope: Manual review of the nine remaining phase/orthogonal synchronization interfaces in p2112.

rows.query: Inspect Matrix.orthogonalGroup and both transpose-inverse membership equivalences.
rows.result: The real finite orthogonal group matches the displayed two transpose-inverse identities.
rows.gap: Matrix.orthogonalGroup on Fin d over the reals supplies the stated group, including reflections.

comparisons.D5: Use finite square real matrices and the orthogonalGroup convention where star is trivial on real entries, so adjoint is transpose. The two membership equivalences give U U-transpose=I and U-transpose U=I. The source assumes d positive, and imposes no determinant-one condition; specialOrthogonalGroup would change the alignment class.

rows.query: Search orthogonal synchronization loss and inspect orthogonal alignment, Frobenius norm and minimizer predicate.
rows.result: The single-block expression can be written, but the source leaves a free block index and omits the summed aggregation described in prose.
rows.gap: The orthogonal loss still needs resolution of its free block index and missing sum before a global loss can be identified.

comparisons.D9: Preserve literal min over one O in O(d) of n^-1 ||Zhat_j-Zstar_j O||_F^2, with free j and no sum. Adjacent stacked-matrix/phase-loss prose suggests a sum but does not supply a corrected display; do not silently insert it or optimize separate O_j. Use Frobenius norm rather than the default matrix norm, and allow reflections. A minimizer predicate does not resolve the missing aggregation or choose a measurable optimizer.

rows.query: Search matrix-normal synchronization and inspect finite real standard Gaussian, Bernoulli law and joint independence.
rows.result: Independent standard real Gaussian matrix entries and Bernoulli masks can generate the upper-triangle blocks.
rows.gap: The observation law still needs upper-triangle block sampling and transpose completion with the exact shared edge masks.

comparisons.D6: For each j<k one Bernoulli mask multiplies the whole d-by-d block Z_j Z_k-transpose+sigma W_jk; do not sample a separate mask per block entry. Standard matrix-normal with identity row/column covariance means iid real N(0,1) entries, unlike phase complex noise's half variances. All upper-triangle noise blocks and masks are mutually independent; opposite blocks are transposes and diagonal blocks zero. Preserve the auxiliary complex ambient typo without adding imaginary noise or changing transpose to a different construction; both mask and observed blocks are available.

rows.query: Search polar decomposition and truncated SVD; inspect inverse-half functional calculus, nonsingular inverse and orthogonal group.
rows.result: For full-rank B, B(B-transpose B)^-1/2 is a candidate polar factor from existing spectral operations, but no full matching polar API was verified.
rows.gap: The polar map still needs its full-rank factorization and proof that the inverse-half construction equals the SVD factor in O(d).

comparisons.D7: The displayed total domain is followed by a formula assuming full rank; do not extend P to singular matrices on that basis. For nonsingular B the Gram matrix is positive definite and its spectral inverse half is meaningful, not entrywise inverse sqrt. Pair left/right singular vectors to obtain M V-transpose and preserve the full orthogonal group including reflections. The identity fallback belongs to D8's estimator, not this polar-factor definition.

rows.query: Inspect sorted symmetric eigenbasis and block selection; compare leading eigenspace estimator and determinant-conditioned polar rounding.
rows.result: A sorted eigenbasis and row-block extraction support the spectral step; the source-specific rounding still needs construction.
rows.gap: The block estimator still needs top-d eigenspace selection and the exact full-rank polar versus identity branch.

comparisons.D8: Take largest algebraic eigenvalues of the real symmetric nd-by-nd block matrix, not largest absolute eigenvalues or singular vectors of X. Select d orthonormal eigenvectors and each consecutive d-row block U_j. If determinant is nonzero use the full-rank polar factor; otherwise output I_d exactly, without an arbitrary singular polar choice. No measurable tie-breaking/eigensolver is specified. The zero-block fallback is data-dependent and remains separate from the nonsingular polar map.

rows.query: Inspect complex Circle definition, norm-one coercion and exponential reconstruction by argument.
rows.result: Circle represents unit complex numbers, and argument reconstruction gives their phase representation after choosing the source's interval convention.
rows.gap: The unit-circle interpretation is available, with the source's x/z binder mismatch and conversion to phases in [0,2pi) kept explicit.

comparisons.D1: The source set binds x but writes |z|=1; Circle matches the accompanying prose's unit complex numbers, without rewriting that quotation. Complex argument reconstruction uses its principal argument convention, so a negative angle may need a 2pi shift to obtain the requested half-open [0,2pi) representative. No independent phase per comparison is implied; the later identifiability group is a single common phase.

rows.query: Inspect compact Circle instance and continuous-function minimum theorem for the global phase-aligned finite loss.
rows.result: The compact unit circle and continuity of the finite squared-distance sum supply existence of a minimum after expressing the objective.
rows.gap: The loss still needs the finite normalized squared-distance objective and its continuity over a single global phase.

comparisons.D4: Minimize n^-1 sum_j |zhat_j-zstar_j a|^2 over one a in Circle, not separate phases a_j or arc distance. n is positive, and the squared absolute value is Euclidean complex distance. The inspected compact minimum theorem supports attainment without uniqueness; it does not itself supply a closed-form alignment or a measurable chosen phase.

rows.query: Inspect Gaussian real variance parameter, product laws and independent upper-triangle masked phase observations.
rows.result: Two independent N(0,1/2) variables form the specified complex Gaussian, and independent masks complete the raw edge model.
rows.gap: The phase observation law still needs complex Gaussian assembly, independent upper-triangle masks and Hermitian completion.

comparisons.D2: Use W=X+iY with independent real components of variance 1/2, so the complex squared norm has mean 1; a real standard Gaussian on the two-dimensional complex plane without scaling would double it. For j<k masks/noises are mutually independent, X_jk is zero when missing, lower entries are conjugates and diagonal zero. Observed data include both A and X; do not center/divide by p or assume independence of mirrored entries. Signal is z_j conjugate(z_k), and p,sigma may vary with n.

rows.query: Search phase spectral normalization and inspect complex Hermitian eigenbasis plus unit-circle norm constraint.
rows.result: The leading eigenvector can be selected through Hermitian spectral infrastructure; coordinatewise phase rounding remains an explicit branch.
rows.gap: The phase estimator still needs a leading-eigenvector choice and coordinate normalization with the exact zero-coordinate fallback.

comparisons.D3: Choose the eigenvector for the largest algebraic eigenvalue of Hermitian X, not largest modulus; use the complex version of the symmetric linear-map spectral theorem. For each nonzero component return u_j/|u_j|, and for zero return 1. Plain complex division at zero gives zero and would violate Circle, so preserve the branch. The source does not specify measurable choices at eigenvalue ties; global phase ambiguity is handled by D4 rather than a silently fixed phase convention.
